heroHeadline: Myla Depot Death Toll Rises to 38 as Russia Threatens 'Massive' Strikes on Ukraine's Energy Grid
heroSubtitle: The confirmed death toll from the Aug 28 Russian drone strike on an ammunition depot in Myla, Kyiv Oblast — the war's deadliest single attack of 2026 — rose to 38 by Aug 30, including the mayor of nearby Dmytrivka, with 20 injured and 4 still missing; Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office widened its criminal negligence probe into munitions storage near residential areas. The same day, Russia's Defense Ministry announced it is preparing 'massive strikes' on Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter, framed as retaliation for a record month of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. Overnight into Aug 31, Russia struck Kyiv and the village of Pohreby with a Kh-59 cruise missile and 121 drones, injuring six people and sparking warehouse fires — the fourth straight night of sustained bombardment of the capital region. Russian military losses reached ~1,488,200 since 2022 per the Ukrainian General Staff, an increase of ~1,600 in the latest 24 hours.
